extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, institutional officials, grant applicants, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A roundup of NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and reminders relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards. Includes pointers to new formats, scoring/process changes, and initiative announcements that affect applicants and awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate experimental models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose the model(s) that best answer the research question rather than adopting models for trend or convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 (Collaborative International Research Projects) application format and features
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PF5 overview to understand required application formatting, award structure, and post-review handling (including splitting into linked awards). Viewing the video will help applicants format and organize submissions consistent with the new PF5 structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for applicable proposals, follow the 2026 pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH. This is the current expected template/format for pilot DMS plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider replication and reproducibility in study design, methods, and proposed analyses. NIH has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative and highlighted topics to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts; incorporate relevant plans or justification where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is scored in the middle third, it may be labeled 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND) under emergency review modifications. Applicants receiving CBND should interpret this as being above triage but not discussed during the meeting; consider this when planning resubmission or next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review and its operational effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). The consolidation is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that peer review procedures and timelines may be affected by centralization. Understand any new CSR-led processes or notices (e.g., guide notices) that change how applications are assigned, reviewed, or processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactivation of NIH small business funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Seed Fund (Small Business Program) is back in action, signaling opportunities for innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses and entrepreneurs should monitor NIH notices and program announcements for reopened solicitations, eligibility requirements, and application instructions for the Seed Fund and related small business programs.
